name: LeadPerch – Chat Contact Form & Lead Capture Widget
author: Kiyaanix

sections.description:
LeadPerch helps you turn website visits into conversations. It adds a simple floating chat-style contact form to your site, making it easy for visitors to ask a question without searching for a contact page.

Every message is saved in your WordPress dashboard, so you have one place to review and manage enquiries. You can also send instant notifications to your team by email, Slack, or a webhook used by your other business tools.

This plugin is a practical choice for small businesses, agencies, service providers, online stores, and anyone who wants a clear way for visitors to get in touch.

What LeadPerch helps you achieve

  • Give visitors an easy, visible way to contact you from any page.
  • Capture more sales leads, support questions, booking requests, and general enquiries.
  • Keep a record of every message inside WordPress.
  • Alert the right people straight away, so enquiries are less likely to be missed.
  • Keep the widget consistent with your brand using your company name, message, colours, and screen position.
  • Reduce unwanted submissions with built-in spam protection and rate limiting.

Key features

  • Floating chat-style contact widget for your WordPress site.
  • Custom company name, greeting, teaser message, colours, and left or right screen position.
  • Dashboard list for viewing, searching, updating, and deleting submissions.
  • Email notifications for new messages, including multiple recipients, optional CC, and optional BCC recipients.
  • Slack incoming-webhook notifications.
  • Generic webhook notifications for connecting to CRM, automation, or other business tools. Webhooks can be signed with a secret for verification.
  • Logged-in visitor auto-fill: use the visitor’s WordPress account name and email when available.
  • Honeypot spam protection, per-IP rate limiting, and an optional submission cooldown.
  • Privacy tools that work with WordPress’s personal-data export and erase screens.
  • Optional automatic deletion of old submissions and a choice to remove plugin data on uninstall.
  • Optional “Powered by” credit link. It is off by default and only appears if you turn it on.

Support the plugin

LeadPerch is free. If it helps your business, you can support its development by turning on the small “Powered by” link at the bottom of the chat widget in LeadPerch > Settings > General. It is entirely optional, off by default, and you can turn it off again at any time. A rating or review on WordPress.org is also greatly appreciated.

Source code

The chat widget script included in this plugin (assets/leadperch.js) is compiled and minified from human-readable source code, which is publicly available at:

https://github.com/kiyaanix/leadperch

To rebuild it yourself:

  1. Clone the repository and run npm ci to install the build tools (Vite).
  2. Run npm run build:embed.
  3. Copy dist-embed/leadperch.js to this plugin’s assets/ folder.

All other plugin files (PHP, admin JavaScript, and CSS) are included in their original, unminified form.

Third-party libraries bundled with this plugin:

  • React and React DOM 18.3.1 (MIT) – https://github.com/facebook/react – included in assets/leadperch.js.
  • Zod 3.25.76 (MIT) – https://github.com/colinhacks/zod – included in assets/leadperch.js.
  • Select2 4.1.0 (MIT) – https://github.com/select2/select2 – included in assets/vendor/select2/ and used on the settings screen.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Upload the plugin ZIP file and activate LeadPerch.
  3. Go to LeadPerch > Settings.
  4. Add your company name, greeting, colours, and notification details.
  5. Visit your website to see the floating widget. Test it by sending yourself a message.
sections.faq:
Is this a live-chat service?

LeadPerch is a chat-style contact widget. Visitors can leave a message and their contact details, then you or your team can reply using your normal email or support process. It does not provide real-time agent-to-visitor messaging.

Where can I see visitor messages?

Go to LeadPerch > Submissions in your WordPress dashboard. You can review messages, search the list, update their status, or delete them.

Can I notify more than one person by email?

Yes. Add multiple recipient addresses separated by commas or semicolons. You can also use the Add CC and Add BCC links for optional copy recipients.

Can I send notifications to Slack or another service?

Yes. Add a Slack incoming webhook URL to post messages in Slack. For another service, add its webhook URL in the Webhook section. If the receiving service supports verification, you can also set a signing secret.

Does the plugin save messages in my WordPress database?

Yes. Submissions are saved in your site’s WordPress database and can be managed from the dashboard. You can choose how long to keep them with the retention setting.

How does the plugin help with privacy requests?

The plugin connects with WordPress’s built-in Tools > Export Personal Data and Tools > Erase Personal Data features for submission data. Review your privacy policy and choose a retention period appropriate for your site.

Does the plugin set any cookies?

One. When a visitor closes the teaser message above the chat icon, the widget sets a first-party cookie named leadperch_teaser_dismissed so the teaser stays hidden for 24 hours. It stores only the value 1. It contains no personal data, is not used for tracking or analytics, and is never sent to external services. It is a functional (preference) cookie that is only set after the visitor clicks the close button. If your site uses a cookie-consent tool, you can list it under functional or preference cookies.

How does spam protection work?

The plugin includes a hidden honeypot field for basic bot detection and can limit the number of submissions from an IP address. You can also set a cooldown period after a successful submission.

Why am I not receiving email notifications?

The plugin uses WordPress email delivery. First, confirm that the recipient address is correct and that email notifications are enabled in LeadPerch > Settings. If messages still do not arrive, your web host may need SMTP configured. An SMTP plugin or your hosting provider can help with reliable delivery.

Does the plugin send visitor data to external services?

No, not by default. The chat widget makes no third-party requests, and visitor IP addresses and countries are determined on your own server. Data only leaves your site through notification channels you set up yourself: email, a Slack incoming webhook, or a webhook URL you enter.

How is the visitor’s IP address and country recorded?

By default the plugin uses the IP address your web server sees (REMOTE_ADDR), and no country is recorded. If your site is behind Cloudflare, a load balancer, a reverse proxy, or AWS CloudFront, choose that option in LeadPerch > Settings > Visitors & Spam > How visitors reach this site. The plugin will then use the visitor IP and country that the service passes along. Only choose a proxy option if your site really uses one, because otherwise visitors could fake their IP address.

Does the plugin add a credit link to my site?

Not unless you choose to. The “Powered by” link is off by default. You can turn it on in LeadPerch > Settings > General with the option “Show a ‘Powered by’ link to support the plugin”.

After your site has received 10 submissions, administrators see a one-time notice on the plugin’s own admin pages asking whether they would like to turn the credit on. You can choose Yes, show the credit, Remind me later (asks again after 30 days, at most twice), or Never show again. The notice is never shown on other admin pages or to visitors.

What happens when I uninstall the plugin?

By default, submissions and settings are kept when the plugin is deleted. Enable the Delete all stored submissions and settings when this plugin is uninstalled option if you want the plugin to remove its data during uninstall.
